notes.text: (b) a second mock token was not available (nothing may be deployed in this round), so the second-token refund is covered by the unit test wrong_token_is_refunded_and_changes_nothing only.

The first run of L6 expected ERR_NO_RECEIPT_FOR_BYTES / ERR_BAD_SIGNATURE for the tampered claim and the edited registration, but ran them AFTER the claim. The contract checks the order status first (STABLECOIN.md section 4), so it answered ERR_ALREADY_CLAIMED / ERR_ORDER_NOT_OPEN. That was my script ordering mistake, not a contract fault: the two failed checks were replaced by the observed (documented) results, and L6b repeats the tamper beats on an open order.

The first L11 attempt registered S1-21..S5-21 (five real orders, per-order storage charge 2460000000000000000000 yocto = 246 bytes each, all equal) and then crashed while saving because my script put a BigInt into the JSON. Those five txs are kept in this log. L11 was re-run with the orders T1-21..T5-21 so the before/after account figures could be recorded.

The shop's first attempt to register N123-21 (tUSDC) failed with ERR_INSUFFICIENT_FREE_BOND: after L10 the shop had withdrawn all but about 5 tUSDC of its bond, so the 6 tUSDC reservation did not fit. That is the contract working, not a bug; the script (my mistake) did not top the bond up first. The failed tx stays in this log; L12b tops the bond up and repeats the registration.

My first L6r expectation was wrong and the script recorded it as a FAIL: I expected 249 bytes x 10^19 yocto (246 + 3 headroom) for order R611-21, but the shop was charged 253 bytes (2530000000000000000000 yocto). Cause: R611-21 has a 7-character id, L11's 246 bytes were for 5-character ids, and the id is stored twice (storage key and record), so 2 extra characters add 4 bytes (246 + 4 + 3 = 253). The contract was right, the expectation was mine. The check below replaced the failed one with the corrected expectation (the observed value is unchanged), and L6s measured the 249-byte case with a 5-character id (T6-21). The transaction itself (register_order R611-21) is recorded as it happened.
